design.independence_note: jobs inside a batch are correlated observations and are never treated as independent inferential replicates
design.order: scenario, load and architecture orders are counterbalanced by batch-seed parity
design.split: fixed group-aware 60/20/20 split; identical complete vectors remain in one partition
design.test_access: held-out test is evaluated once after each selected subset is frozen

resources.monolith_allocation: 6/concurrency CPU and 12/concurrency GiB per simultaneous container

quality_thresholds.origin: rounded below the medians observed in the completed 30-seed X-CANIDS architecture campaign

primary_hypothesis: At concurrency 4, 8 or 16 and equal aggregate resources, G-FShield increases the paired batch count of jobs reaching the scenario quality threshold within 1080 seconds.
secondary_hypotheses: G-FShield increases qualified solutions per minute and completed jobs per minute as concurrency grows.
G-FShield increases completed IWSSR evaluations per second under concurrent load.
Held-out macro-F1 of completed jobs remains within a 0.01 non-inferiority margin.

analysis.summary: median paired difference with 95% bootstrap interval
analysis.test: exact or Monte Carlo paired sign-flip permutation test
analysis.multiplicity: Holm correction within prespecified metric families
analysis.censoring: unreached quality thresholds are censored at 1080 seconds

interpretation_constraints: A throughput advantage does not imply lower single-request latency.
Failure of jobs at high concurrency is part of capacity behavior unless caused by an infrastructure or instrumentation fault.
No claim of horizontal scalability or fault tolerance follows from this fixed-node load experiment.
Pilot seeds and pilot outputs are excluded from confirmatory analysis.
